hypothesis: E35x (frozen, 16 seeds) found the augmented kernel LOWER than the first-order one at b = 0 (geometric mean 0.82 at M = 512, 0.73 at M = 2048; interval of the mean log ratio excludes 0) although there is no latent. The augmented model is a mixture of the kernel and its reflection with shared parameters, so its E-step feeds the kernel every sequence and its mirror image, and the b = 0 truth is reflection-symmetric. Hypothesis: the gain is the use of the symmetry, not the latent state.
design: New driver, importing E35's data builders unchanged (same training chains, validation and test bundles, same initialisation as the first-order arm). b = 0 only; M in (512, 2048); seeds 0-15. Arms: em_first_order_sym (the first-order kernel fitted on the sequences and their mirror images, nothing else) and em_first_order_2m (the first-order kernel on twice as many INDEPENDENT sequences: the control for 'only more data'). Comparators: E35x's frozen em_first_order and em_augmented, same seeds and bundles (hashes compared at read time; E35x ran on the cluster and the hashes are platform-specific, so E46 runs there too). Two shards of eight seeds (e46-s0, e46-s8), defq.

predeclared_predictions.P1: The symmetrised first-order kernel matches the augmented one: the 95% bootstrap interval of the mean per-seed log(sym / augmented) contains 0 at both M.
predeclared_predictions.P2: The mirror data alone give the gain: the interval of the mean log(sym / first-order) lies entirely below 0 at both M.
predeclared_predictions.P3: Reflection is at least nearly as good as doubling the data: the upper end of the interval of the mean log(sym / 2m) is below log 1.1 at both M.

predeclared_analysis: symmetry.csv merged over the two shards plus E35x's frozen b = 0 rows; per (M) the paired per-seed log ratios; bootstrap by Monte Carlo (200,000 draws, seed 20260912) on the mean log ratio; at_cap and converged read beside every risk; read by tools/make_extension_numbers.py.
provenance_note: Written after E35x was read (that is what motivated it) and before any E46 cell ran; the explanation tested is a hypothesis, and a falsified P1 would mean the gain comes from something else, which would then be the open question.
resources: cluster, defq, 2 x 8 cpus, 24G, 8 h; about 0.4 h per fit at M = 512 and 1-2 h at 2048 (twice the chains)

outcome.P1: FALSIFIED, and in the direction that strengthens the hypothesis: the symmetrised first-order kernel is not equal to the augmented one, it is BETTER. Mean log(sym / augmented) = -0.190 [-0.280, -0.105] at M = 512 (geometric ratio 0.827, sym lower in 14/16 seeds) and -0.169 [-0.298, -0.058] at 2048 (0.844, 12/16).
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED. Mean log(sym / first-order) = -0.390 [-0.619, -0.214] at M = 512 (ratio 0.677, sym lower in 16/16) and -0.490 [-0.755, -0.271] at 2048 (0.612, 15/16): the mirror data alone give the whole gain E35x saw, and more (E35x: augmented / first-order 0.82 and 0.73).
outcome.P3: FALSIFIED as written, by the interval's width, not by the estimate. Mean log(sym / 2m) = -0.137 [-0.500, +0.139] at M = 512 and -0.075 [-0.347, +0.187] at 2048; the registered criterion was an upper end below log 1.1 = +0.095. The seed-mean risks are the same: 0.0162 (sym) against 0.0161 (2m) at 512, 0.0066 against 0.0066 at 2048; sym lower in 8/16 seeds at both sizes, per-seed ratios 0.10-2.25 (heavy seed-to-seed variation).
outcome.unregistered: Seed-mean risks (first-order / sym / augmented / 2m): M = 512: 0.0211 / 0.0162 / 0.0191 / 0.0161; M = 2048: 0.0099 / 0.0066 / 0.0076 / 0.0066. Doubling the data with independent sequences gives log(2m / first-order) = -0.253 [-0.418, -0.088] and -0.416 [-0.641, -0.170]. Using the reflection of every sequence is, in seed mean, as good as drawing as many new sequences again; the augmented model's mixture of the kernel and its reflection captures about 60-70% of that gain (it adds a responsibility to estimate per sequence). Fits at the last checkpoint (first-order sym / 2m): 3 and 3 of 16 at 512, 5 and 7 at 2048 (E35x first-order / augmented: 1/2 and 2/4). Reading: the b = 0 gain of the augmented kernel is the reflection symmetry of the truth, not the latent state; a first-order fit on the data and their mirror images is the cheaper and better way to use it.
